players.product: ThinkSystem AI servers (Neptune liquid cooling) and AMD Helios racks

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025/26 results (year to March 31, 2026, annual report): record revenue US$83.1 billion, up 20%; gross profit margin 15.4%, down 0.7 points mainly on product mix and lower ISG profitability; profit attributable to equity holders US$1.9 billion, up 38%, and adjusted profit attributable US$2.0 billion, up 42%; AI-related revenues up 105% to 33% of Group revenue, with triple-digit growth in AI devices and AI services and high double-digit growth in AI servers. Fourth fiscal quarter: revenue US$21.6 billion (+27%), adjusted net income US$559 million (+101%), AI-related revenues +84% to 38% of revenue. R&D expenses US$2,490,403 thousand; ISG restructuring charges US$285 million (intangible and construction-in-progress impairment, severance); capital expenditure US$1,859 million (US$1,151 million), mainly patents and technology, assets under construction and equipment held for lease.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025/26 revenue US$83.1 billion (+20%); adjusted profit attributable US$2.0 billion (+42%); capex US$1,859 million

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025/26 business groups (annual report): IDG revenue US$58.9 billion (+17%) at a 7.2% operating margin, with a record fourth-quarter global PC share of 24.4% (+1.3 points), premium PCs at 50% of Q4 shipments and a cumulative 1.1 billion PCs sold; smartphones posted record full-year revenue since acquisition, premium mix 19% of shipments, and Motorola became the number one flip-foldable brand. ISG revenue a record US$19.2 billion (+32%) with a full-year operating profit of US$73 million (operating loss US$68,501 thousand a year earlier); Q4 ISG revenue US$5.6 billion (+37%) and its highest-ever quarterly operating profit of US$202 million. SSG revenue US$10 billion (+19%) with operating profit US$2.2 billion. By geography China +16%, EMEA +21%, Americas +21%, Asia Pacific +23%; Lenovo reached number two in the North America PC market in Q4 with a 20.4% shipment share.
quarterly_data.figure: IDG US$58.9 billion (+17%); ISG US$19.2 billion (+32%), operating profit US$73 million; SSG US$10 billion (+19%)

quarterly_data.signal: AI infrastructure (annual report): the AI server pipeline expanded to US$21 billion exiting FY2025/26; Lenovo's NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 platform achieved full shipment support in the fourth fiscal quarter and next-generation Rubin-based platforms are targeted for time-to-market in the second half of calendar 2026; more than 5,800 AI customer deployments delivered, supported by annual capacity of more than 70,000 racks and direct liquid-cooled server capacity of more than 11,000 racks. The Lenovo AI Factory enables deployment-ready environments with time to first token of approximately 90 days and sub-1.1 PUE. The Infinidat acquisition (high-end enterprise storage) completed in early April 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: AI server pipeline US$21 billion; capacity more than 70,000 racks per year, more than 11,000 direct liquid-cooled racks

quarterly_data.signal: Customer and supplier concentration (annual report): Lenovo sold less than 27% of its goods and services to its five largest customers in FY2025/26; the largest supplier accounted for 10% and the five largest suppliers combined 39% of purchases.
quarterly_data.figure: five largest customers less than 27% of sales; largest supplier 10%, five largest suppliers 39% of purchases

quarterly_data.signal: Component shortage and working capital (annual report): inventories rose 48% to US$11,720,885 thousand at March 31, 2026, mainly from a higher raw-materials inventory level in response to the industry-wide component shortage, which has driven up component cost, as the Group strives to source more components to meet higher demand (raw materials and work-in-progress were more than 60% of inventories); the cash conversion cycle lengthened to 17 days from 2; bank deposits and cash US$4,983 million and net cash US$242 million; contracted capital commitments for property, plant and equipment US$287,823 thousand (US$89,648 thousand).
quarterly_data.figure: inventories US$11,720,885 thousand (+48%); cash conversion cycle 17 days

quarterly_data.signal: Strategy and outlook (annual report, management): Lenovo expects agentic AI to fuel exponential inferencing growth as AI shifts from model training toward real-time decision-making, increasing demand for validated hybrid AI platforms; it rolled out its Qira cross-device personal AI super agent in April 2026; in the CSP segment it deepened relationships with key hyperscalers and expanded its customer base. Management says it faces a highly volatile environment with supply chain disruptions, geopolitical tensions and a rapidly evolving AI landscape, and keeps a global footprint of more than 30 manufacturing sites across 10 markets.

connects_to.relationship: AI infrastructure supply, deployment and managed services

contracts.signal: Lenovo annual report case study: NScale, an AI infrastructure provider building a new AI factory in Iceland, selected Lenovo and NVIDIA to help deploy the site; Lenovo supported the project through its AI infrastructure solutions, deployment capabilities and services, including deployment and managed services, helping NScale implement a repeatable architecture for the Iceland AI factory.
